adjudicator: Claude Code (read-only human-equivalent read of both value strings and, for borderline pairs, both source snippets)

sample.population: 76 C-vs-B free_text disagreement pairs (codebook type == free_text)

label_definitions.SAME_FACT: Same substantive content, different wording. Includes formatting, abbreviation, tense, delimiter, singular/plural, and granularity (one arm carries a detail the other drops, with no conflicting claim).
label_definitions.DIFFERENT_FACT: A reader would extract a different value — a conflicting number, a different metric, a different limitation, or a positive claim against an absence claim.
label_definitions.UNCLEAR: Cannot be resolved as either from the two values plus their snippets.

variance_tags.note: Descriptive only, on SAME_FACT pairs. Not used by the rule.
variance_tags.granularity: one arm carries a detail the other drops
variance_tags.formatting: punctuation, delimiter, case, spacing, tense, singular/plural
variance_tags.abbreviation: expanded vs abbreviated form of the same referent

rationale.445::secondary_outcomes: Numeric conflict, not framing. B 'Number of mistakes: Less than one mistake per sample' vs C 'Mistakes: <2 per sample'. B also claims leak pressure was 'significantly better than all other techniques' while C's own snippet says the burst pressure 'is comparable to these other techniques'. Completion time is a relative claim in B and an absolute 50.0 +/- 14.7 min in C.
rationale.460::secondary_outcomes: Different metric set from the same table. B reports four rates (FN 0.0%, FP 0.0%, grasp failure 3.6%, multiple grasp 5.2%); C reports 'Average number of replanning steps: 10.58' — a metric absent from B — and keeps only FN. Overlap is one of four items.
rationale.549::comparison_to_human: Different metric selected from the same snippet, which contains both. B reports the path-length reduction (~50%); C reports task completion time (39.3s vs 45.7s). C additionally attaches a p-value (p=0.003) that does not appear in its snippet.
rationale.663::key_limitation: Two unrelated limitations. B: 'The system does not provide needle steering, which limits accuracy in tissue with variations in density causing needle deflections.' C: 'Reliance on US imaging with lower resolution compared to other modalities.' Note the crossover — B's value is what C's snippet supports, and neither snippet supports C's value.
rationale.694::secondary_outcomes: Positive claim against absence claim. B 'Confidence level: Improved with stiffness variation' vs C 'Confidence level: NR'. B's snippet ('They mention success rates and confidence levels in nodule depth estimation') does not support the improvement claim; C has no snippet at all. Whichever is right, the two cells assert opposite things.
rationale.764::secondary_outcomes: Conflicting pose-error value. B 'Pose error: 6.44 +/- 8.59 mm' vs C 'pose error: within 9.00 mm'. B's own snippet says 'The average tracking errors along the X and Y axis are within 9.00 mm' — C's figure, not B's; 6.44 +/- 8.59 appears in neither snippet. Contact force (0.99 +/- 0.68 N) is identical modulo PDF digit spacing.
rationale.386::secondary_outcomes: Allocation, not wording, and not obviously a different fact. B 'Accuracy: 1.30 +/- 0.44 mm; Accuracy: 1.54 +/- 0.34 mm' vs C 'Accuracy: 1.54 +/- 0.34 mm; Force: Not reported; Success rate: Not reported'. The shared snippet carries both numbers; C put 1.30 in primary_outcome_value and 1.54 here, while B duplicated both across the two fields. No numeric conflict — the arms extracted the same numbers and split them differently between fields, and C added two explicit absence declarations. Cannot be called pure wording variance, cannot be called a different value.
rationale.466::key_limitation: Shared head clause, diverging tails. B 'The system currently operates in controlled environments without real-time feedback.' vs C 'The approach works in controlled environments without considering unpredictable factors.' The identical snippet says only 'our current results were obtained in controlled and predictable environments'. C's tail restates the snippet; B's 'without real-time feedback' is a separate deficit the snippet does not mention. The limitation identified is the same; the elaborations are two different claims.
rationale.516::robot_platform: Identical leading clause, incompatible qualifiers. B 'No physical platform — computational simulation of a 6-DOF gripper' vs C 'No physical platform — Algorithm on existing platform'. Both answer the field the same way (no hardware). B's snippet supports simulation of a 'generic 6-DOF gripper'; C's qualifier implies an existing platform was used, which the snippet does not support. Same answer to the field, materially different claim about the setup.
